# Errors reference

Every error is a real HTTP status with a problem-details body (RFC 9457), `Content-Type: application/problem+json`. Every response, an error or not, carries the header `X-Correlation-Id`: the value the request sent in that header, or one the gateway made. The same value is in the body and in the access line of the request (see [Logs reference](/docs/reference/logs/)), so one value finds both.

The fields of the body:

- `type`: what kind of error, as an address under `https://slay400.dev/problems/`; `about:blank` for a request the listener refused by itself (413, 414).
- `title`: the kind in words, the same for every error of that type.
- `status`: the HTTP status.
- `detail`: only when there is something to add: the program's message for a program error, the count of problems for an invalid request.
- `instance`: `urn:slay400:request:` and the correlation ID.
- `code`: the program's error code, for a program error only.
- `errors`: for an invalid request, one entry per problem: the `field`, a `code` and a `message`.
- `tenant` and `environment`: once the gateway knows them.
- `correlationId`: as in the header.

Nothing of IBM i reaches a body: no message ID, library, job, or text of an escape message. The access line names the problem, and the gateway's warnings give more for the operator.

Each response below was recorded from the gateway by a test of this repository, with the mock backend of the `shop` example. The 500 and the 502 come from a stub of the program call, since a mock cannot produce them. Where the gateway made the correlation ID itself, it is written `<generated>`.

The Community Edition never answers 401 or 403: authentication is not part of it.

## 400 The request is not valid

A parameter is missing, has the wrong type, is too long, or the body is not JSON. `errors` lists every problem at once, so that one correction fixes them all. Correct the request: the OpenAPI document of the bundle says what each operation takes.

<!-- snippet: examples/reference/errors/request-invalid.http -->
```http
HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
Content-Type: application/problem+json
X-Correlation-Id: example-request-invalid

{"type":"https://slay400.dev/problems/request-invalid","title":"The request is not valid","status":400,"detail":"The request has 1 problem; see errors.","instance":"urn:slay400:request:example-request-invalid","errors":[{"field":"quantity","code":"REQ007","message":"Body field must be a whole number"}],"tenant":"acme","environment":"test","correlationId":"example-request-invalid"}
```

## 400 Request line or headers too large

The request line or the headers are over the listener's limit. The listener answers before the request reaches the pipeline, so the body has no tenant or environment and the correlation ID is one the gateway made. Send fewer or shorter headers.

<!-- snippet: examples/reference/errors/request-too-large.http -->
```http
HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
Content-Type: application/problem+json
X-Correlation-Id: <generated>

{"type":"https://slay400.dev/problems/request-invalid","title":"The request is not valid","status":400,"instance":"urn:slay400:request:<generated>","correlationId":"<generated>"}
```

## 404 Not found

No tenant, environment or route matches the address, or the bundle of the route was removed. Check the address against `/<tenant>/<environment>/<route>` (see [URLs and routes](/docs/reference/urls-and-routes/)). The body names no tenant or environment when they are the part that did not match.

<!-- snippet: examples/reference/errors/not-found.http -->
```http
HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found
Content-Type: application/problem+json
X-Correlation-Id: example-not-found

{"type":"https://slay400.dev/problems/not-found","title":"Not found","status":404,"instance":"urn:slay400:request:example-not-found","correlationId":"example-not-found"}
```

## 404 or another status: the program reported an error

The program reported a business error, and the error mapping of its `api.yaml` gives this error code its own status (`statusByCode`); here `E404` is answered with 404. The body is the one of a program error (422 below), with the status of the mapping.

<!-- snippet: examples/reference/errors/program-error-mapped.http -->
```http
HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found
Content-Type: application/problem+json
X-Correlation-Id: example-program-error-mapped

{"type":"https://slay400.dev/problems/program-error","title":"The program reported an error","status":404,"detail":"Order not found","instance":"urn:slay400:request:example-program-error-mapped","code":"E404","tenant":"acme","environment":"test","correlationId":"example-program-error-mapped"}
```

## 405 Method not allowed

The route exists, but not for this method. The header `Allow` lists the methods it takes.

<!-- snippet: examples/reference/errors/method-not-allowed.http -->
```http
HTTP/1.1 405 Method Not Allowed
Allow: GET
Content-Type: application/problem+json
X-Correlation-Id: example-method-not-allowed

{"type":"https://slay400.dev/problems/method-not-allowed","title":"Method not allowed","status":405,"instance":"urn:slay400:request:example-method-not-allowed","tenant":"acme","environment":"test","correlationId":"example-method-not-allowed"}
```

## 413 Request body too large

The body is over the listener's limit. The listener answers as soon as it reads `Content-Length`, without reading the body.

<!-- snippet: examples/reference/errors/payload-too-large.http -->
```http
HTTP/1.1 413 Request Entity Too Large
Content-Type: application/problem+json
X-Correlation-Id: <generated>

{"type":"about:blank","title":"Request Entity Too Large","status":413,"instance":"urn:slay400:request:<generated>","correlationId":"<generated>"}
```

## 414 Address too long

The request line is over the listener's limit of 8 KiB.

<!-- snippet: examples/reference/errors/uri-too-long.http -->
```http
HTTP/1.1 414 Request-URI Too Long
Content-Type: application/problem+json
X-Correlation-Id: <generated>

{"type":"about:blank","title":"Request-URI Too Long","status":414,"instance":"urn:slay400:request:<generated>","correlationId":"<generated>"}
```

## 422 The program reported an error

The program ran and reported a business error through the convention of its `api.yaml` (`error`): `code` and `detail` are the program's error code and message. The default status of a program error is 422; the mapping can set another one.

<!-- snippet: examples/reference/errors/program-error.http -->
```http
HTTP/1.1 422 Unprocessable Content
Content-Type: application/problem+json
X-Correlation-Id: example-program-error

{"type":"https://slay400.dev/problems/program-error","title":"The program reported an error","status":422,"detail":"Order refused","instance":"urn:slay400:request:example-program-error","code":"E999","tenant":"acme","environment":"test","correlationId":"example-program-error"}
```

## 500 Internal server error

Something failed inside the gateway that it did not expect. The body says nothing of the cause; the gateway logs the access line with status 500. If it happens again, report it with the correlation ID.

<!-- snippet: examples/reference/errors/internal-error.http -->
```http
HTTP/1.1 500 Internal Server Error
Content-Type: application/problem+json
X-Correlation-Id: example-internal-error

{"type":"https://slay400.dev/problems/internal-error","title":"Internal server error","status":500,"instance":"urn:slay400:request:example-internal-error","tenant":"acme","environment":"test","correlationId":"example-internal-error"}
```

## 502 The program call failed

The program call failed: the program is missing, the sign-on was refused, IBM i returned an escape message, or the program returned data the API cannot represent. The body does not say which; the gateway's warning does, without values.

<!-- snippet: examples/reference/errors/program-call-failed.http -->
```http
HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
Content-Type: application/problem+json
X-Correlation-Id: example-program-call-failed

{"type":"https://slay400.dev/problems/program-call-failed","title":"The program call failed","status":502,"instance":"urn:slay400:request:example-program-call-failed","tenant":"acme","environment":"test","correlationId":"example-program-call-failed"}
```

## 503 Service unavailable

The environment cannot call a program right now: the IBM i is not reachable, or every connection of the pool is in use. Try again later; if it lasts, check the system and `pool.maxConnections`.

<!-- snippet: examples/reference/errors/service-unavailable.http -->
```http
HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
Content-Type: application/problem+json
X-Correlation-Id: example-service-unavailable

{"type":"https://slay400.dev/problems/service-unavailable","title":"Service unavailable","status":503,"instance":"urn:slay400:request:example-service-unavailable","tenant":"acme","environment":"test","correlationId":"example-service-unavailable"}
```

## 504 The program did not answer in time

The program did not answer within `callTimeoutSeconds` of its environment. The call is given up; what the program did on IBM i is not undone.

<!-- snippet: examples/reference/errors/program-timeout.http -->
```http
HTTP/1.1 504 Gateway Timeout
Content-Type: application/problem+json
X-Correlation-Id: example-program-timeout

{"type":"https://slay400.dev/problems/program-timeout","title":"The program did not answer in time","status":504,"instance":"urn:slay400:request:example-program-timeout","tenant":"acme","environment":"test","correlationId":"example-program-timeout"}
```
